For category c, compute one paired effect per sampled user: d_cu = diagnostic score − reference score, using the same training prefix, target and candidates. Aggregate as Δ = (mean(d_1) + mean(d_2) + mean(d_3) + mean(d_4))/4; pooling users would overweight larger categories. Bootstrap users with replacement independently within each category, preserving pairs and category sample sizes; recompute Δ for each replicate and report its 2.5th–97.5th percentiles. Keep categories fixed: the estimand concerns these four categories. This follows [stratified resampling](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/boot/html/boot.html) and [paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) principles.

Suggested operational rules, not universal statistical thresholds: require ≥30 unique eligible users per category/slice before reporting an interval, and flag sparse or constant effects. Five users/category supports descriptive diagnostics only. Report eligible counts, sampled counts and exclusions. If any category is missing or below threshold, mark the four-category slice estimate/interval unavailable; label any available-category summary separately. Bound GPU work with a prespecified equal user cap, one prefix/user, inference mode, bounded batches and candidate chunks. Cache paired scalar outcomes, then run thousands of bootstrap replicates on CPU without model refitting. Keep diagnostic candidate sampling distinct from the pinned benchmark and preserve full-catalog recommendations where required.

Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted checkpoints, chosen prefixes and candidates; they omit training-seed variability and generalization to new categories. Repeated validation-guided search introduces selection optimism that ordinary bootstrap intervals do not correct ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Treat diagnostic effects as hypothesis-generating, not predicted HR@10 gains; reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation.
